title: Most People in Japan Still Value Handwriting
paragraphs: Today, many people write using computers and smartphones. But in Japan, most people still think handwriting is important, according to a new survey.
The national survey was done by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, a part of the government. The results were shared on October 2, 2026.

The survey found that 80.4% of people think the habit of writing by hand should be kept. This is still a very large number of people. But it is lower than in a similar survey 11 years ago, when the number was 91.5%.

Many people also feel that handwriting is special. About 68.2% said handwriting can show a person's character and feelings in a way that computer fonts cannot. In addition, 82.3% said they prefer letters and cards that are written by hand. However, many people also said they are happy with printed letters if they include a short handwritten message.

Interestingly, young people seem to care a lot about handwriting. Teenagers, who grew up with smartphones, gave the strongest support of all age groups. About 84.8% of teenagers said that the value of handwriting must not become smaller in the future.

Japanese writing uses thousands of different characters, called kanji, as well as two other writing systems. Because people now type more, some people worry that they are forgetting how to write some kanji by hand.
The survey shows that, even in a digital age, many people in Japan still see handwriting as an important part of their culture.
